# @ternent/ledger

> Standalone signed append-only history. Staging and committed history are distinct.

Published interface baseline: `npm install @ternent/ledger@0.2.0-alpha.1 @ternent/identity@0.6.0-alpha.1`.
[Public README](https://github.com/ternent/core/blob/main/packages/ledger/README.md).
Declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`, `dist/protocol/index.d.ts` and referenced types.

## Create, stage, commit and reopen

```ts
import { generateSigner } from "@ternent/identity";
import { createLedger, encodeJson, verifyLedger } from "@ternent/ledger";
const created = await generateSigner();
if (!created.ok) throw new Error(created.error.code);
const log = await createLedger({ signer: created.value });
await log.create();
await log.append({ kind: "reading", payload: { value: 21 } });
const preview = await log.replay();
await log.commit();
const snapshot = await log.export();
const bytes = encodeJson(snapshot);
const report = await verifyLedger(bytes);
if (report.integrity !== "valid") throw new Error("Invalid history");
const reader = await createLedger();
await reader.import(bytes);
const committed = await reader.replay({ includeStaged: false });
```

`create()` immediately signs genesis. `append`/`appendMany` stage entries; `commit`
signs them together. `export()` returns a committed snapshot object, not bytes;
`encodeJson` converts it to portable bytes. `load(snapshot)` accepts an object;
`import(bytes)` accepts the encoded container. Failed operations preserve history
and staged work. Loading while staged rejects DRAFT_PENDING. `clearStaged()` drops
staging. Staging is volatile and never exported.

Replay includes staged entries by default; each item marks committed and commitId.
Use includeStaged false for committed reconstruction. Optional `initialProjection`
and synchronous pure `projector(projection, entry)` derive application data.
`getState()` is detached/frozen; `subscribe()` observes successful changes;
`destroy()` closes the handle. Callbacks must not reenter the mutation queue.
Validation/signing failures reject Fault with a structured finding; projector errors
propagate. This differs from Concord's structured mutation results.

## Trust and composition

Root exports lifecycle, payload helpers and protocol helpers. `/protocol` exposes
canonicalize, encodeJson, parseJson, inspectLedger, verifyLedger, compareLedgers,
hashLedgerEntry, hashLedgerCommit and ledgerSignatureMessage without the lifecycle.
Verify original imported bytes; do not parse/reserialize with JSON.parse first.
Ledger verifies the full signed linear history and signer/author binding. It has no
membership policy: a supplied signer can append to a valid log. Use Concord for
application authority, encrypted groups and command semantics.

Portable JSON uses safe integers (no fractions, unsafe integers or negative zero),
valid Unicode, dense arrays and plain objects; closed record schemas apply. Use
these APIs for canonical bytes, IDs and signatures rather than recreating them.
compareLedgers reports equal/ahead/behind/diverged/unrelated, without merging or
selecting a head. A valid signature does not establish freshness.

## Optional encryption

`encodePayload(data, codec)` and `decodePayload(data, codec?)` compose explicit
byte codecs such as Armour's createAgeCodec. Decode yields plain, decoded or locked.
Raw replay still returns the stored envelope at entry.payload.data. Missing codecs
never invent plaintext. Ledger neither distributes keys nor automatically decrypts.
Keep secrets, storage, synchronization and draft recovery with the host.
